homonyms.none: no other noun with this form

examples.text: Die Aubergine in Scheiben schneiden und salzen.
examples.tr: Slice the aubergine and salt it.

examples.text: Auf dem Markt gab es heute schöne Auberginen.
examples.tr: There were nice aubergines at the market today.

synonyms.nuance: the usual word in Austria (from Italian melanzane)

etymology.text: Unadapted borrowing from French aubergine (from Catalan albergínia, from Arabic al-bāḏinjān). Doublet of Melanzani.

funFacts: English eggplant and old German Eierfrucht both come from early white, egg-shaped varieties.
pitfalls: French spelling and sound: -gine is said like French [ʒiːnə]; plural Auberginen.
subtleties: The same vegetable has an Arabic name behind it in almost every European language: aubergine, berenjena, albergínia.

homonyms.none: no other noun with this form

senses.def: pumpkin, squash, gourd (any plant of the genus Cucurbita or its fruit)

examples.text: Aus dem Kürbis kochen wir eine Suppe.
examples.tr: We're making a soup from the pumpkin.

examples.text: Die Kinder schnitzen Gesichter in die Kürbisse.
examples.tr: The children carve faces into the pumpkins.

examples.text: Im Garten wachsen dieses Jahr riesige Kürbisse.
examples.tr: Huge pumpkins are growing in the garden this year.

profile.synonymsNone: No everyday synonym; varieties have their own names (Hokkaido, Butternut).

etymology.text: From Middle High German kürbiȥ, Old High German kurbiȥ, from Proto-West Germanic *kurbit; cognate with Yiddish קירבעס (kirbes).

funFacts: Kürbiskernöl, the dark green pumpkin-seed oil, is a speciality of Styria in Austria.
pitfalls: -is doubles the s before an ending: des Kürbisses, die Kürbisse.
subtleties: German uses one word, Kürbis, where English has pumpkin, squash and gourd.
